title: Cabinet & Interior Refresh in Cinco Ranch, Katy: Case Study
description: See how a 7-day cabinet refinish and downstairs repaint in Cinco Ranch, Katy took a 15-year-old kitchen from dark and dated to bright, cohesive, and new.
author: Chris Petkau
imageAlt: Refinished white kitchen cabinets, an example of professional cabinet painting results near Katy, TX
content:
Refinishing dated kitchen cabinets and repainting the entire downstairs of a Cinco Ranch home in Katy, TX took our crew seven days, and it turned a fifteen-year-old kitchen into one the homeowner says she smiles at every time she walks in. Here is exactly what that project involved, from the cabinets to the color system to what she told us when the crew packed up.

What Was Wrong With This Cinco Ranch Kitchen?

Amy's kitchen was a classic Cinco Ranch story. The home was more than fifteen years old, and the kitchen still had its original finish — paint that had started chipping in the high-touch spots, cabinets that had gone from a warm, contemporary choice in the mid-2000s to something that just read dark and dated next to the rest of the house. In her own words, it had been fifteen-plus years and it was showing every one of them: chipped, out of style, and no longer the room she wanted to spend her mornings in. It is one of the most common calls we get across the Katy-Fulshear corridor. Cinco Ranch, Cross Creek Ranch, and the other master-planned communities across the Katy service area are full of homes built in that same window, and a lot of those original kitchens are due for exactly this kind of refresh — you can see more of that transformation in our cabinet painting portfolio.

What Did the Project Include?

This was not a cabinets-only job. Along with a full professional cabinet refinishing in Katy, we repainted the walls, the ceilings, and every door throughout the downstairs. That scope matters more than it sounds like on paper. A kitchen can get a beautiful new cabinet finish and still look unfinished if the walls around it are the same tired builder color and the doors leading in and out are scuffed and yellowed. Bringing the whole downstairs into one paint system at the same time is what lets the new cabinets actually read as the centerpiece of a finished home, instead of a nice kitchen surrounded by everything that did not get touched. It also meant one crew, one schedule, and one walkthrough at the end — instead of stretching the same disruption to a household across two or three separate projects. It is the same prep-first approach behind our painting preparation process and every job listed under our cabinet painting services.

Why the Sherwin-Williams Gallery System?

We ran this entire project on the Sherwin-Williams Gallery Series, chosen for the durability it holds up on cabinets and on the doors and trim that get touched, bumped, and cleaned the most in a home. Cabinets went in Snowbound, a clean, bright white with just enough warmth to avoid feeling clinical. Walls went in Site White, a soft, warm neutral that gives the room depth without competing with the cabinets. Trim and every downstairs door went in Extra White, the crispest of the three, which is what makes the cabinet color and the wall color both look intentional instead of mismatched. Three whites, each doing a different job: Snowbound carries the cabinets, Site White warms the walls, and Extra White sharpens every edge, door, and piece of trim in between. Used together, they give a kitchen like Amy's contrast and dimension instead of flattening the whole downstairs into a single shade of white. If you are staring down a similar decision between several near-identical whites, our color consultation service is built around exactly that kind of call.

How Long Does a Project Like This Take?

Start to finish, this project took seven days — a realistic timeline for a full cabinet refinish paired with a downstairs repaint of the walls, ceilings, and doors. A professional sequence like this moves through the same core phases on every job: protecting the space and prepping every surface, repairing any imperfections in the existing cabinet and wall finish, priming so the new coats bond properly instead of sitting on top of old paint, then applying a spray-grade finish on the cabinets for the smooth, factory-level result that brushing and rolling cannot match, and closing out with a full walkthrough alongside the homeowner. Seven days is enough time to do all of that correctly across an entire downstairs, without rushing the cure time a finish like this needs to hold up. It is a similar rhythm to what we walk through on any interior painting project, and our interior painting prices page breaks down what typically moves a downstairs repaint toward the longer or shorter end of that range.

What Did the Homeowner Think?

Amy sat down for a video testimonial after the crew finished, and what she said is the reason we do this work. She told us she did not know paint could make her so happy — that she never thought something so little could be such a mood changer. Now she says she walks into her kitchen and just smiles. Beyond the finished look, what she kept coming back to was how the crew worked: punctual every day, communicating clearly about what was happening and when, and paying attention to details most homeowners would not even think to ask about. More than once, the crew came back to help with something outside the original scope, without a hint of reluctance about it. That is the standard we hold every crew to on every interior painting project in Katy, not just the ones that end up as a case study, and it is why you will hear the same things from homeowners across our client testimonials.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long does cabinet refinishing take in Katy?

It depends on the size of the kitchen and how much else is included alongside the cabinets. Amy's combined cabinet-and-downstairs project took seven days; a cabinets-only project is often shorter. Our cabinet pricing page breaks down what typically affects that timeline and cost.

Can I stay in my home during a cabinet and interior project?

Yes. We section off and protect the areas we are working in each day so the rest of the home stays livable, and we sequence the work to keep disruption manageable throughout the project.

Should I paint trim and doors at the same time as cabinets?

We recommend it whenever the budget allows. Doing the cabinets, walls, ceilings, and doors together — the way we did in Amy's home — is what makes the finished space read as one cohesive room instead of a new kitchen next to everything that still looks old.

How do I choose between white cabinet colors?

It comes down to how the white pairs with your walls, trim, and lighting. Snowbound, Site White, and Extra White each read slightly differently, which is why we bring samples to the estimate and look at them in your own kitchen's light before locking anything in.

Is refinishing worth it on 15-year-old cabinets?

If the cabinet boxes are structurally sound — which most are at that age — refinishing gives you a new look without the cost or disruption of full replacement, backed by our 2 & 5-Year Written Warranty. Amy's kitchen is a good example of what that refresh can look like.

If your own kitchen is starting to feel like Amy's did, Chris will walk it with you in person, give you a straight read on whether your cabinets are worth refinishing, and put an itemized scope in writing before any paint goes on.
